summary: Flathead County, MT tower dated 1933 as a 30' pole L-4 tower; firelookout.com gives destruction in 1977; listed gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: firelookout.com gives 'Destroyed 1977'; the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as Gone with no date; no source describes what remains

events.note: firelookout.com dates the 30' pole L-4 tower to 1933
Hungry Horse News (August 24, 1951) reports a repair trip to the building and tower
September 1973 lightning storm caused 25 new fires; the largest was in the Forks Lookout area, per the Daily Inter Lake

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com places the lookout in Glacier National Park, 13 miles north of Whitefish; the Forest Lookouts page and the 1973 Daily Inter Lake item place it in the Flathead National Forest (Glacier View Ranger District). The record keeps Flathead National Forest; the Glacier Park attribution is recorded as a disagreement.
firelookout.com gives destruction in 1977; the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower only as Gone, with no date.

notes_for_editor: The 1933 build year and 1977 destruction rest on firelookout.com alone; two searches found no second source. The agency conflict (Glacier National Park vs Flathead National Forest) is unresolved. The creek name is spelled Hallowat in the title and Hollowat in the text. Height of 9.1 m is converted from the listed 30' pole. Elevation on firelookout.com is 6497' but has no facts key. Hungry Horse News and Daily Inter Lake archives could confirm the 1977 removal.
